Historical Preservation Loans
This project is a new program designed to create a loan fund for historical preservation loans. The loans would be limited to residential structures. The maximum loan would be $15,000 and the interest rate would be 7%; no grants would be available. Only structures in the Central and Alum Rock Planning Areas which are designated as historically significant by City ordinance or State action would qualify. Minimal staff assistance would be available. The property owner would be required to obtain his own contractor; rehabilitation staff would only make an initial inspection to identify hazards and a final inspection to insure satisfactory completion. The program would provide 8 to 1 leverage; therefore, $25,000 per year would provide $200,000 in loans. The program is proposed for the 5th and 6th years only.
Rehabilitation Service (All Target Areas)
This project provides the staffing for all loan and grant programs. The staff in the 4th year is increased over current staffing by one rehabilitation specialist. With this staffing level, services can be provided for 179 jobs in the 4th year (see Chart 2). In the 5th year, an additional rehabilitation specialist, 2 rehabilitation technicians and 1 typist-clerk will be added to the staff.
Relocation
This project will provide funding for anticipated permanent and temporary relocations in all target areas.
Meadowfair Neighborhood Park
This project will provide for the completion of park construction, street improvements and lighting of tennis courts. Work will include a revision of the existing master plan due to the elimination of the elementary school site adjacent to the park.
Alum Rock Senior Citizens Center
This project provides funding in the amount of $33,000 to match a $70,159 grant from the Council on Aging. The funds would be used for a Senior Citizens Center. The proposed location is in the vicinity of King and McKee. The project will involve either acquisition and rehabilitation of a building for use as a Senior Citizens Center or construction of additional rooms at Plata Arroyo Neighborhood Center for this purpose.
